query: How does resolution time vary across category, priority, and assignment group?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: A finer-grained category derived from short_description gives a genuine grouping axis for resolution-time analysis. Overlaps somewhat with the existing 'category' column, but appears more specific and text-derived. Values are sound readings of the descriptions.

per_column.name: failure_symptom_type
per_column.rationale: Symptom type is a new orthogonal axis not in original columns and plausibly correlates with resolution time. Samples map cleanly from descriptions (e.g. 'Cannot connect'->cannot_connect), though 'service_down' for 'not working properly' is a reasonable but softer inference.

per_column.name: affected_system
per_column.rationale: Maps incidents to affected system, a useful modelling axis. Values track descriptions well, though it is largely collinear with incident_category (email->email_server etc.), slightly reducing independent leverage.

per_column.name: scope_indicator
per_column.rationale: Scope (individual vs enterprise vs department) is a strong analytical axis potentially explaining resolution time. However groundedness is weaker: 'Email system not working properly'->enterprise_wide and generic 'VPN connection issue'->remote_access are inferred beyond what the text states. Department cases are grounded, but many assignments are unsupported confident specifics.

per_column.name: is_self_resolved
per_column.rationale: Self-resolution is relevant to resolution time, but the value basis is unclear; the sample 'Internet connectivity issue' marked True is not clearly warranted by the source text provided (only timestamps/description). Large NULL share suggests weak derivability.

per_column.name: has_assigned_agent
per_column.rationale: Directly derivable from the existing 'assigned_to' column, making it largely redundant. Grounded, but adds little new analytical leverage for resolution-time comparison across assignment group.

per_column.name: incident_open_status
per_column.rationale: A restatement of existing 'state'/'closed_at' columns. Grounded (closed rows -> False) but trivially redundant, offering minimal new axis for the query.

per_column.name: caller_user
per_column.rationale: Essentially a restatement of the existing caller_id and is not part of category/priority/assignment-group analysis. Grounded but adds no analytical leverage for this query.

judge.rationale: Several added columns (failure_symptom_type, affected_system, scope_indicator, incident_category) supply genuine new grouping axes beyond category/priority/assignment_group and are mostly well-grounded in the short_description. Others (has_assigned_agent, incident_open_status, caller_user) are redundant restatements of existing original columns and add little. Groundedness is generally solid for text-extracted categories, but scope_indicator and is_self_resolved make confident inferences the source text does not clearly support, warranting some penalty.
